newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pub, restaurant buys shove King Food up.
newsitem.headline: Pub, restaurant buys shove King Food up.

text.p: King Food Holdings's announcement it had bought pub and restaurant chains pushed it to a new year high on Wednesday in fairly large volumes.
Dealers said the news it had purchased franchised pub chains Keg and McGinty and franchised restaurant chain Saddles had been received with glee by the market.
"Its the good news that anyone holding (King) shares has been waiting for. The guys pumped the share up and it could be bought some more," one dealer said.
Shares jumped to a new year high of 192 cents in early trade, up 12 cents or 6.7 percent, but by 0906 GMT had fallen down to 178 cents with 113,400 shares changing hands.
Another dealer said that the slip could be due to profit-taking but added that King's failure to disclose the purchase price might be worrying some investors.

Keg and McGinty have been bought from Keg Franchising South Africa (Pty) Ltd with effect from May 1, 1997 and Saddles was acquired from Saddles Steak Franchising (Pty) Ltd with effect from March 1, this year.
The new chains bring the total number of King Food's outlets to 208, including Mike's Kitchen, Mike's Pantry, Bimbos and Porterhouse.
King said the acquisitions would make substantial contributions to profit for the year ending February 1998.
